added_lemmas.statement: In the published model of Dwivedi et al., an exogenous quantity is generated independently of all other sources of randomness, equation (4) generates each potential outcome from treatment-indexed exogenous unit and time factors plus exogenous noise, and the model expressly requires the counterfactual at a decision time not to depend on past treatment.

source.locator: pages 2382--2383, definition of exogenous, equation (1) discussion, and equation (4)

attestation.note: Checked against the accepted-version source and PDF; the equation and published pagination agree.

added_lemmas.statement: Dwivedi et al.'s published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) give a high-probability squared-error bound for their nearest-neighbor estimator of one treatment-specific mean counterfactual at a fixed unit and time under their Assumptions 1--5.

attestation.note: Checked against Theorem 3.1 and its displayed bounds in the accepted-version PDF.

added_lemmas.statement: Dwivedi et al.'s published Assumptions 6--7 permit bounded coordinatewise Lipschitz nonlinear functions of exogenous unit and time factors supported on a compact cube with lower-bounded time-factor density, and their Theorem 4.1 gives the corresponding unit-by-time nearest-neighbor error bound under Assumptions 1, 2, 4, 6, and 7.

attestation.note: Checked against Assumptions 6--7 and Theorem 4.1 in the accepted-version PDF.

proposed.statement: Fix \(q<1/4\) and the amplitudes in \(\mathrm{def:markov\mbox{-}witness}\). For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), the bounded Markov law \(W_\ell\) lies in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n_\ell,m_\ell}(1,1,1,q,B,\theta\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell})\), but its arm means depend on \(A_{i,j-1}\), so it is not generated by the exogenous unit and time factors in Dwivedi et al.'s published equation (4) on page 2383. Conversely, their published Assumption 6 on page 2397 and Theorem 4.1 on page 2398 contain the bounded Lipschitz nonlinear-factor law generated by \(f^{\mathrm D}_0\), \(f^{\mathrm D}_1\), \(u^{\mathrm D}\), and \(v^{\mathrm D}\), for which \(\operatorname{rank}(M^{\mathrm D})=\min(n,m)\) almost surely; this law is excluded by \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\) for fixed \(r\). Thus their unit-by-time nearest-neighbor bound in published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389 and the normalized maximum-row IPW-SVD frontier are non-representable in either direction.
proposed.justification: This gives the exact model-theoretic separation from the closest adaptive pooled unit-by-time factor result.
proposed.gap: Dwivedi et al., published Theorem 3.1 and equations (17)--(18) on page 2389, control a nearest-neighbor unit-by-time arm-mean error under the factor structure in equation (4) on page 2383, not a row-subspace loss under treatment-path-dependent arm means.
proposed.consumer: Referees can distinguish the row-factor target and predictable-mask domain from published adaptive counterfactual imputation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses three published comparator facts, so the target's dependency metadata must declare the corresponding cited leaves.
